### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **113** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**77** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b20695e193c1eed3a01b6ca5f1dcb8ec4a7acb7e` — the merge of head `6b3a8286e6ba18016b5d9d3f2a3d29cd84e2925f` into base `6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b20695e193c1eed3a01b6ca5f1dcb8ec4a7acb7e && git checkout b20695e193c1eed3a01b6ca5f1dcb8ec4a7acb7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b 6b3a8286e6ba18016b5d9d3f2a3d29cd84e2925f && git checkout -B drift-repro 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b && git merge --no-ff 6b3a8286e6ba18016b5d9d3f2a3d29cd84e2925f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6abcb72b0f20257b075149a1fabcaba884648b8b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6b3a8286e6ba18016b5d9d3f2a3d29cd84e2925f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/plugin-install.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts, packages/core/src/security/plugin-artifact-integrity.ts, packages/core/src/security/plugin-artifact-signature.ts, packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-lifecycle-health.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-trusted-key.object.ts, docs/adr/0025-plugin-package-distribution.md (read, not reviewed). The remainder of the diff (cli commands and utils, runtime stores, platform-objects object and tests, changesets, census, README, lifecycle.mdx) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #27123 (body + all 10 comments, ruling `6467932167` letter B′, claim `6469792198`, os-dev-report `6480186227` at the earlier head `70cdda4e`), PR #27335 body + 37-file list + `git diff origin/main...cr-27335` at merge-base `ebfadb02`, and the check-runs on the head. The check-runs are the gate verdicts: every completed run is `success` or path-`skipped` (`Lint UI`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, opt-in harnesses); none failed. All ten required contexts report `success` except `Lint UI`, which is `skipped` because no `ui/` path moves. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size` are green. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay login to name.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_trusted_key` (`platform-object-names.ts:92`). Derived: `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` gains one member and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName('sys_trusted_key')` flips false → true. Readers on the head, each judged:
   - `stack.zod.ts` ~L4704 (`validateCrossReferences`): an action whose `objectName` is `sys_trusted_key` was refused at the merge-base and is admitted on this head. RIGHT: the object is registered unconditionally by `PlatformObjectsPlugin`'s first manifest on this head (`plugin.ts:197`, `objects: [SysMigration, SysMigrationJournal, SysSecret, SysTrustedKey]`), and the registry's maintenance contract is exactness. Leaving the row out would make a real platform object a refused reference, which the registry header names as worse than the heuristic it replaced, and `platform-object-names.test.ts` ("registers exactly the objects each package declares") reds the omission since `sys-trusted-key.object.ts` declares the name.
   - `packages/lint` rung ③ (`validate-object-references.ts:238`, `validate-nav-access.ts:162`, `validate-translation-references.ts:1848`): a reference to `sys_trusted_key` is now a known platform object instead of an advisory probable-typo. RIGHT, same ground.
   - `engine-lifecycle-health.ts:107` (`resolvePrimaryDatasource`): the new name now votes when registered. RIGHT: it rides the same manifest as `sys_secret` with no `defaultDatasource` triple (`plugin.ts` keeps the three siblings' no-triple rule, test pins `infra.defaultDatasource` undefined), so it binds where `sys_secret` binds and cannot split the primary.
   - `dangling-reference-audit.ts:383` derives from the `plugin-security` group only; unaffected. RIGHT.
   - `organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts:123-156` requires an inventory row per registered object; the diff adds the `sys_trusted_key` row (fate `column-drop`, as `sys_secret`). RIGHT.
   - `@objectstack/spec` `api-surface`: the export's declared type (a readonly record of string to readonly string array) does not move; a value member is added. The gate (`check:api-surface`, in the green `TypeScript Type Check` job) agrees. RIGHT that nothing on the export surface moves.
2. Clause-② direction on item 1 (ruled here, as the at-tier review owns the direction): the widening of the reference-resolution accept set is DERIVATIVE of the object's registration in `platform-objects`, not a relaxation of the spec's own authorable vocabulary; the registry is a name list that tracks what the platform registers, and no metadata key, accepted value or type is added. The declared `Clause-②: no` stands. For the record, a `yes (widening)` reading would move neither the level (`none` kind ⇒ `patch` either way) nor the tier (already `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the schema face). The PR body and the spec changeset both disclose the row in their ② line, which is the right form.
3. `manifest.zod.ts`: `PluginIntegritySchema` TSDoc and the `ManifestSchema.integrity` field TSDoc are rewritten; the `.describe()` strings are byte-identical on both sides (`'Per-file content digests of the plugin artifact (ADR-0025 §3.2)'`), `PluginIntegritySchema` stays `z.record(z.string(), z.string())`, the field stays `.optional()`, and `PluginPackagingSchema` / `PluginRuntimeSchema` are untouched on this head. Derived: no accept-set change, no served-body change, no generated-docs change (`check:docs` and `check:generated` in the green `TypeScript Type Check` job agree, and the dev's `check:generated --fix` reported 14/14 current). RIGHT.
4. `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`: the `integrity` row flips `dead` → `live` with in-repo evidence `install.ts#PluginInstall` and `publish.ts#PluginPublish`; `state-counts/manifest.md` moves 27/14 → 28/13 and `liveness/README.md`'s manifest row stops counting `integrity` among the dead. The anchor class `PluginInstall` exists on the head and calls `verifyIntegrity` before any write; `Spec property liveness` is green. RIGHT. The row's own note had reserved the flip for whatever built unpack-time re-verification, which this PR is.
5. Public surface outside spec, named for completeness (lane seat's files, judged only for the registry row's truth): new deployment-level object `sys_trusted_key` (`tenant: false`, `manage_platform_settings`, engine-owned, API `get`/`list` only, unique indexes on `key_id` and `fingerprint`); nine new `@objectstack/runtime` exports; four new CLI commands. Observation: `SysTrustedKey` is not imported into `packages/platform-objects/scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` (which imports `SysSetting, SysSecret, SysSettingAudit, SysMigration` from `system/index`), so its labels are outside `en.objects.generated.ts` and outside the coverage ratchet's population (that ratchet is rooted on extract configs, so `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-coverage` are green by construction). Four sibling deployment-level objects (`sys_platform_setting`, `sys_platform_setting_audit`, `sys_migration_journal`, `sys_metadata_activation`) share the omission on `main`, so this is precedent-consistent and not a hits finding; carried as a should-fix note for the lane seat under ③.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27123-integrity-reverified-at-unpack.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/core` patch; `Clause-②: no — …`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches the diff: the spec change is TSDoc prose plus one registry-row value; core is comment prose only. `none` kind ⇒ `patch` by the Post-Task Checklist rule; the `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json` versions spec/core/cli/runtime/platform-objects together regardless.
- `.changeset/27123-local-plugin-install.md`: `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch; `Clause-②: no — …`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Matches: new commands, stores and a system object are platform code, no authorable surface moves (`check:authorable-surface` green). Level follows the kind (`none` ⇒ `patch`), as the rule prescribes even for a feature.
- `Check Changeset` green on the head. The PR body carries the same two line-initial declarations.
- `Clause-②:` line: `no` is correct as ruled in ①.2; no `(narrowing)` arm, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed. The card's own caveat (`PluginPackagingSchema` narrows to `bundled`) belongs to slice 3 and does not occur on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (PR body "Known limitations") and report fields (`open_questions: []`, two `out_of_scope_findings`), each answered or escalated:

1. Installations file read-modify-write takes no lock (two concurrent installs on one project/env can drop a record; the write itself is temp-file + rename). ANSWERED: accepted for M1 (local, first-party, operator-driven); should-fix, carried to card #27123 for slice 2, which reads the same file at boot and is the right place to decide a lock or an append-only record. Not a hits file.
2. gunzip has no size cap before the signature check. ANSWERED with a sharper note: `verifyPublisherSignature` (`plugin-artifact-signature.ts:204`) needs only the raw artifact bytes, the `.sig` string and the key, and `parseSignature` yields the `keyId` without the manifest, so the signature step can precede `readTarGz` entirely (the `package_id`/`version` fields feed only the platform counter-sign, which M1 sets `requirePlatform: false`); the one cost is booting the trust store before inflating. Should-fix for slice 2 or a follow-up; for M1 T0 the artifact is the developer's own, so this is not a must-fix. Not a hits file.
3. Two projects that installed identical bytes share ownership of one dir; slice 2's loader is to check the kept artifact sha against the record. ANSWERED: accepted; carried to card #27123 as a slice-2 acceptance line.
4. `out_of_scope` 1: ADR-0025 v2 §3.5 still says "Steps 4–7 do not exist … there is no `os plugin install`" (read on `main`, L293-296). ESCALATED: the card's Tier H docs follow-up now owes three edits, not one — the §3.5 M1 ✅ line, the §7 dated note the ruling `6467932167` ordered, and this sentence. Correctly left out of the PR (no `docs/adr/**` path on the file list; queue guard green).
5. `out_of_scope` 2: text collision with #27246 on `plugin.ts`'s first manifest, `plugin.test.ts`'s roster and `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`. ANSWERED: noted; whichever lands second also owes its own `platform-object-names.ts` row, which `platform-object-names.test.ts` enforces, so the union cannot land silently wrong.
6. Reviewer's flag (from ①.5): `SysTrustedKey` outside the platform-objects i18n extract config. ESCALATED as a should-fix note for the lane seat on card #27123, precedent-consistent with four siblings; a fix is one import line plus a bundle regeneration, better done once for all five.
7. Size: 3096 changed lines (+3016 / −80, generated included) exceeds the 3,000-line human-merge threshold; the PR body says so. Landing is Tier H by size (an authorized APPROVED review and the owning seat, or the maintainer's merge or enqueue) whatever this record says; this PASS clears the contract-review leg only. `needs:contract-review` comes off with this record.
8. `open_questions: []` — none to answer. Premises 1–3 of `6464984121` were re-run by the dev on `9ff8154c` and hold on this head as read (`verifyPluginArtifact(` has exactly two call sites on the branch: its definition and `install.ts`).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`** — judged against ADR-0025 v2 §3.2 / §3.5 M1, ruling `6467932167`, card item 5, and the first consumer `install.ts`.

- Claim "RE-VERIFIED AT UNPACK BY `os plugin install` … re-hashes the unpacked files against the map before it materializes anything": HOLDS. `install.ts` step 2 calls `verifyIntegrity(files, manifest.integrity, { exempt: [MANIFEST_FILENAME, SIGNATURE_FILENAME] })` over the in-memory archive entries, before the signature step, the record read, and `materializePlugin`; `materializePlugin` writes exactly that `files` array (`plugin-install.ts`, `for (const file of input.files) … writeFileSync(target, file.data)`), so the hashed bytes are the written bytes.
- Claim "refuses the install by name on the same three findings": HOLDS. `verifyIntegrity` emits `digest_mismatch` / `missing_file` / `extra_file`; install refuses `integrity_mismatch` with one `formatIntegrityViolation` line per finding and exits 1; `publish.ts:141` runs the identical call with the identical `exempt` set, so the two readers agree on the covered set. A non-object map is refused earlier as `integrity_malformed`, a fourth refusal the TSDoc need not name since the schema already types the map as a record.
- Claim "an absent map is the same permissive pass there": HOLDS. `verifyIntegrity` returns `{ ok: true, skipped: true }` on `undefined`/`null`; install prints "per-file check skipped". Consistent with the field staying `.optional()` and with the ADR's "artifacts predating integrity computation stay publishable".
- Claim "sits beside the install's signature check over the whole artifact, and neither replaces the other": HOLDS. Step 3 verifies the detached `.sig` with `verifyPluginArtifact` over the raw compressed bytes; a present signature is always verified (`--trust-unsigned` only covers an absent one); a tampered artifact whose map was rewritten to match is caught by the signature, and a corrupt-but-signed one by the map — the two mechanisms are independent, as the text says.
- Claim "The cloud control plane stores the artifact blob opaquely and checks nothing against the map": carried over from the prior text (cross-repo, unmeasured here, as the liveness row's `_note` already records); the sentence narrows nothing and adds no new assertion about cloud.
- Card acceptance "the listed self-descriptions are deleted in the same PRs; no new NOT ENFORCED prose is added": HOLDS for this slice. The "NOT RE-VERIFIED AT UNPACK … there is no `os plugin install`" block and the field's "enforce leg is unbuilt" sentence are gone; `PluginRuntimeSchema`'s "nothing dispatches on the tier" is deliberately left, still true until slice 2 (the loader), as the claim `6469792198` scopes it.
- Break attempts: an `integrity` map whose values are not strings is coerced via `String()` and mismatches → refused; a map naming the exempt `objectstack.plugin.json` is skipped at both readers, matching `computeIntegrity`'s exclusion; an archive entry named `artifact.osplugin` (the kept original) is refused as reserved by `archiveEntryProblems` before step 2. No path makes the TSDoc false. No must-fix, no should-fix on this file.

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`** — judged against the registry's own maintenance contract, its conformance gate, and the registering code.

- The row's claim is "`@objectstack/platform-objects` registers `sys_trusted_key`". HOLDS on the head: `sys-trusted-key.object.ts` declares `ObjectSchema.create({ name: 'sys_trusted_key', … })`, `plugin.ts` registers it in the first (`com.objectstack.platform-objects`, `scope: 'system'`) manifest unconditionally, and `plugin.test.ts` pins the four-object roster and the absence of the routing triple. The gate that enforces the row (`platform-object-names.test.ts`, a source scan of every `*.object.ts` per owning package) and the row are one change and were read as one; `Test Core` is green.
- Placement: inside the `platform-objects` group, once, alphabetical between `sys_team_member` and `sys_two_factor`; the test sorts, so order is cosmetic. Every registered name carries the `sys_` prefix, as the test requires.
- Scenario it is accepted against (ruling B′: the install command resolves a signature's key id in `sys_trusted_key` through a one-shot boot that composes `PlatformObjectsPlugin`): the registry row makes a stack reference to the object resolve and lets the lifecycle-health vote count it; neither path is on the install's critical path, and both are correct as judged in ①.1.
- Break attempts: a second package declaring the same name would red the conformance test (one-owner membership); a deployment that composes no `PlatformObjectsPlugin` sees the name unregistered and the health vote abstains by design ("no evidence either way"). No must-fix, no should-fix on this file.

**Verdict on ④:** no must-fix on either `hits` file. Should-fix items (lock, signature-before-inflate, i18n config import) are all in lane-seat files or future slices and are carried to the card under ③.
